conviction_note: The print turns on US clinical visits against IDEXX's own H2 assumption of about -1.5%. The broad Vetsource/CATalyst series for Jul-Sep came in at -1.9%, a little worse, while IDEXX's record of beating the bar and a full-year EPS consensus sitting below the guided low end lean the other way. These roughly offset, so p_up is 49 on an abs move of 7.5 (the option-implied 8.06, nudged down because the last three reactions were small at 3.6, 0.0 and -4.6). The findings sum to -0.7 and the scaled number is -0.15. They agree in sign. The sum is larger because the visits finding is sized on its own and is not netted against the beat history.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS $3.71 and revenue about $1.19B, whisper EPS $3.82 (Earnings Whispers, 2026-10-26: https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/IDXX/21350). Company guide cross-check from primary documents: FY2026 revenue guide $4,700-4,745M (Q2 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000874716/000110465926090033/tm2622041d1_ex99-1.htm) less H1 actuals of $1,141M (Q1 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000874716/000110465926055203/tm2613510d1_ex99-1.htm) and $1,217M leaves an H2 of $2,342-2,387M. Against an H2 2025 of about $2,197M that is +6.6% to +8.6% reported, which puts Q3 at about $1,178-1,200M on Q3 2025's $1,105M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/874716/000110465925105185/tm2530045d1_ex99-1.htm). Consensus revenue therefore sits at the middle of the guide. FY EPS guide is $14.69-14.94 against a consensus of $14.68, just below the low end. Q3 guide from the Q2 call: reported operating margin 32.5-32.8%, organic growth in line with the implied H2 range, a 70bp FX headwind to reported Q3 revenue. The revenue bar is consistent with the company guide. The EPS bar has one estimate source.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest at the 2026-10-15 settlement: 1,929,268 shares, about 2.4% of shares outstanding, 3.62 days to cover. That is down from 2.09M and 4.35 days at 2026-08-31 (https://equibles.com/stocks/idxx/shortinterest), so the short is not crowded and is drifting lower. 25-delta skew is +0.49 vol points (balanced). Put/call open interest is 2.23 on only 681 contracts of total OI in the front expiry. The event-implied move is 8.06%. Into the print the stock is up 8.44% over 20 days, +0.31% over 5 days, 26.7% below its 52-week high and 11.4% above its low. The low was about $501.66, set in September/early October.

findings.finding: The CATalyst Council / Vetsource series (6,595 US practices) shows US clinical visits across all species down 1.9% YoY in Jul-Sep 2026. That is worse than the -1.5% for the 12 months to June 2026 in the same series, and worse than the roughly -1.5% H2 US visit decline IDEXX built into its guide on 2026-08-04, when its own Q2 same-store figure was -1.3%. Puppy visits fell about 10%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Visits are the line this stock has traded on in 2026. On 2026-02-02, a beat with a cautious visit outlook went -4.6% (baseline). On 2026-08-04 the Q2 beat with -1.3% visits went +3.57%. In Nov 2025 a beat-and-raise with stable visits went +14.84%.
findings.why_not_priced: It was published in a vet trade outlet (dvm360) and a cat-focused CATalyst release on 2026-10-13, framed as a feline-share story. No IDEXX preview cites it: the Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-10-26 still anchors on Q2's -1.3% and the company's -1.5% assumption. If it were priced, previews would quote a Q3 visit number and the stock would not have run up 8.4% over 20 days into the print.
findings.independence: Different measurement from IDEXX's own same-store metric, so the gap may be a methodology difference. Same direction: Zoetis Q2 (2026-08-06) said canine pruritic visits fell more than 2% and US companion animal revenue fell 11% (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260805793569/en/). Vetwatch national YTD to late July shows patient visits -2.3% (https://nysvms.org/304553-2/). IDEXX has grown CAG recurring about 10% organic through comparable visit declines, which caps the size of this finding.

findings.finding: Q3 consensus EPS of $3.71 is $0.11 below the whisper of $3.82, and FY consensus EPS of $14.68 sits below the low end of IDEXX's raised $14.69-14.94 guide. IDEXX beat Q2 EPS by $0.33 and Q3 2025 by about $0.26 ($3.40 vs $3.14), so the EPS bar is set for another beat and a raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beat-and-raise paid +14.84% in Nov 2025 and +27.49% in Aug 2025. In 2026 beats bought +3.57%, -0.03% and -4.6%, so the market has recently paid little for an EPS beat alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the beat habit is well known and the whisper is public. What may not be priced is the size of a raise. Consensus below the guide low end means the Street is not underwriting the guide, so a raise from a Q3 beat would push estimates up. If that were fully priced, FY consensus would sit at or above the guide midpoint ($14.81).
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K guide and EPS are in the primary document (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000874716/000110465926090033/tm2622041d1_ex99-1.htm). The consensus number comes from one source.

findings.finding: Tractor Supply's Q3 2026 release and call (2026-10-22) put companion-animal comps at about -2% in Q3, improving from -3% in Q2 and -4% in Q1. That points to US pet-owner spending stabilising through Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No IDEXX reaction history ties to retail pet comps. This is a macro-to-company proxy.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits in a farm-retailer release that IDEXX previews do not cite. If it were priced, sector notes would cite improving pet-spend trends. Instead the only October sector note seen (Jefferies, 2026-10-20) was about pricing risk.
findings.independence: Proxy. Chewy's quarter to 2026-08-02 showed pet health and specialty sales +14% YoY and triple-digit vet-clinic growth (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001766502/000162828026061011/chwyq22026exhibit991.htm). Retail consumables spending is a weak read on clinic diagnostics, and the broader visit series in finding 1 points the other way.

findings.finding: The NYSVMS Practice Pulse survey (n=67, New York only, conducted July 2026, published August 2026) found 13% of practices reporting Q3 revenue up, against 35% a year earlier, and 43% reporting a decrease. On the same page, Vetwatch national YTD-2026 data to late July shows practice revenue +2.7% and patient visits -2.3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same visits line as finding 1. See there.
findings.why_not_priced: A regional member survey that no sell-side preview carries. It is small, self-selected and has a margin of error of about 11-13 points, so it is sized below the broad series in finding 1.
findings.independence: The direction matches finding 1 (CATalyst/Vetsource), but the source is different. Note that Vetwatch's national revenue of +2.7% is far below IDEXX's US recurring growth of about 10%, so practice revenue has not translated into IDEXX's numbers before.

findings.finding: The dollar strengthened late in Q3: EUR/USD broke below its year-to-date low of 1.1325 on 2026-09-29, and BBVA puts the dollar index up nearly 2% in September. On the Q2 call IDEXX said a 1% move in the USD is worth about $8M of revenue and $0.03 of EPS for the rest of the year, so the Q4-implied guide carries a small extra FX headwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX has been a footnote on IDEXX prints. In Q2 a $15M FX cut to revenue was absorbed in a raised EPS guide, and the stock went +3.57%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, since FX is public. Analysts often carry stale FX in models until the company updates them, and if it were fully priced FY revenue consensus would sit below the $4.72B midpoint. Sources disagree on the size of the September dollar move (another source has the DXY +0.2%), so this finding is small.
findings.independence: The IDEXX FX sensitivity comes from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15344824561263616). The rate move rests on one source and is contradicted in size by another.

findings.finding: IDEXX had placed about 2,700 inVue Dx units by midyear against a full-year target of about 5,500, so H2 needs about 2,800. Q3 2026 laps the Q3 2025 launch quarter, and Q2 instrument revenue was already down 20% organically. A soft Q3 instrument line is inside what management flagged.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history. Instrument lumpiness was raised on the Q2 call (BofA), and the stock went +3.57% that day.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, because management guided to it. A placement number well short of a run rate of about 1,400 a quarter would be new. If the market expected a shortfall, previews would flag inVue rather than CancerDx.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview (2026-10-26) notes the -20% Q2 instrument revenue (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/IDXX/21350). Both items rest on company statements.

findings.finding: An Earnings Whispers headline reports that on 2026-10-20 Jefferies downgraded Zoetis and Elanco on animal-health pricing risk and said it prefers IDEXX. This is sector rotation toward IDXX in the 20-day run-up window.
findings.why_not_priced: Likely priced already: it is ten days old and sits inside the +8.4% 20-day run-up. The 'pricing risk' thesis also cuts against IDEXX, which relies on about 4% net price.
findings.independence: Headline only, no detail found. It shares the Earnings Whispers preview text with finding 2.

outside_window.finding: Zoetis expects commercial validation of its Vetscan OmniMax chemistry platform by year-end 2026. This is a competitive threat to IDEXX's Catalyst installed base in 2027, and Zoetis reports Q3 on 2026-11-05, after the exit window.

searched_and_found_nothing: IDEXX EDGAR filings since 2026-08-04: no 8-K, only routine Forms 4/144 (director Kingsley option exercise and sale of 2,203 shares at $532 on 2026-09-04). No buyback, M&A terms or guidance update.
IDEXX September/October investor-conference commentary on quarter-to-date trends: none found
Analyst price-target or rating changes in October 2026: only a KeyBanc initiation at Sector Weight (2026-10-12, StreetInsider headline, no detail)
Monthly (August/September) national Vetsource or Vetwatch visit figures: not found beyond the CATalyst quarterly figure
IDEXX 2027 list-price increase notice: not found
Antech/Mars reference-lab pricing actions in 2026: only speculative commentary
CoVetAI acquisition (2026-09-16): terms undisclosed, immaterial to Q3

rejected_candidates.detail: Filed at -0.2 in the draft. The visit signal is merged into finding 1 as independence, since it is the same visits line seen through a peer. Diagnostics growth at a competitor reads both ways (category strength or share loss).

rejected_candidates.detail: Company-guided catalysts already inside the FY guide and finding 2's beat setup. The revenue effect in Q3 is small and is not filed separately.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Chewy Q2 FY2026 (quarter to 2026-08-02): pet health and specialty +14%, vet clinics triple-digit growth
rejected_candidates.detail: Used as independence on finding 3 (pet-spend stabilisation proxy).

baseline_tension: Balanced skew and a +8.4% 20-day run-up off the September low mean some recovery is priced. The slightly worse Q3 visits series cuts against that run-up, while the beat setup agrees with it. Net, the evidence does not move the coin far from 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the beat/raise-setup finding was cut from +0.8 to +0.5 because 2026 beats bought only +3.6%, 0.0% and -4.6%.

Core table (a finding inside guidance goes toward 0): the inVue/instrument finding was cut from -0.2 to -0.1 and the Jefferies sector-rotation finding from +0.2 to +0.1, since one sits inside guidance and the other is already priced in the run-up.

Rule 5 and 'two readings of one line count once': the draft had a separate Zoetis Q2 visits finding at -0.2 (4th in sizes_pct). It was merged into finding 1 as corroboration and is listed in rejected_candidates as a duplicate. The NYSVMS regional survey was cut from -0.3 to -0.2 so it sits below the broad CATalyst/Vetsource series.

Rules 6 and 7: the bar was checked against the company guide (consensus revenue sits at the middle of the guide-implied Q3 range), and short interest was looked up (not crowded). Neither changed a size.

Net: the draft had 8 findings summing to -0.7 and the emitted set has 7 findings summing to -0.7. The equal sums are a coincidence: the positive cuts (+0.8 to +0.5, +0.2 to +0.1) offset the negative cuts (Zoetis -0.2 merged, NYSVMS -0.3 to -0.2, inVue -0.2 to -0.1). abs_move_pct 7.5 and p_up 49 are unchanged.
